where: OpenAlex harvest run 8: the genus queries and the family review "Scincidae vision review"; titles and abstract starts screened with tools/views/screen_candidates.py, and the stored abstracts of the listed candidates read (the harvest stores up to their first 700 characters)
WebSearch result titles and links (no snippets were returned); nothing was opened, because this round fetches nothing (desk-screen.md point 3)
the older combination Lygosoma indicum (Sphenomorphus indicus, the Indian forest skink) was searched as well (web)
chased: none applies: the queue gives no nearest measured relative (closest = none) for Sphenomorphus fov_h_deg and holds no family or order for the genus, so there is no source to chase; the harvest ran no citation step and searched the family review "Scincidae vision review" instead
note: WebSearch returned result titles and links only (no snippets), so web results were judged by title, and nothing was opened. The tool lists no candidate for this trait. "Sphenomorphus visual field" returned the Wikipedia articles on the genus and on S. maculatus, a figure page of the ZooKeys description of S. tamchucensis, a Raffles Bulletin of Zoology PDF (volume 49, pages 181 to 189), an archive.org scan of a 1967 study of three Bornean Sphenomorphus, a Treubia article, a Zootaxa article (5620.3.8), BioStor 65661 and a Zenodo record (5693929) shown without titles; their titles and hosts point to taxonomic and faunistic works. "forest skink visual field" returned the retina study of the African five-lined skink (Trachylepis quinquetaeniata, PMC10024390) and a library proxy mirror of the same journal (not opened), the 2024 poster from the Université de Mons comparing the eyes of four tropical skinks and its abstract, a Reptiles & Amphibians article (journals.ku.edu), a 2014 Behaviour PDF hosted by Northeastern State University, a Peeref record, a photograph page, a blog page on the banded forest skink (Sphenomorphus melanopogon) and a Malaysian biodiversity species page. "Lygosoma indicum visual field" returned taxonomic papers of the Zoological Survey of India, a 2011 paper on Lygosoma in Indochina, a 2018 Journal of Herpetology description of a new Lygosoma (BioOne and its DOI page), BioStor 281894 and the Reptile Database account of Sphenomorphus indicus. No title names a visual-field measurement for a skink of this genus. The Mons poster compares eye morphology, and its title promises no field width; it is on this unit's wanted list for acuity, fovea and pupil. Main holds no visual-field row for any skink (Scincidae), and Land and Nilsson 2012 (canon, in hand) gives none for a Sphenomorphus on main. The genus's queue rows carry no family or order, so the queue offers no relative. acuity_cpd, fovea and pupil_shape have no record: they wait on the wanted list for the Mons poster, whose four species are not visible, and pupil_shape also waits on a species description and two species accounts that may state the pupil. lambda_max_nm and receptor_classes wait on the wanted list for the 2024 bioRxiv opsin-gene study of Australian cryptozoic skinks, the only work the harvest query "Sphenomorphus spectral sensitivity opsin" returned.
